A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CATransformers and contain readable main text, figures, tables, and complete appendices. Retained material can be matched despite extensive reorganization. Inconsistencies in some new v3 results affect their interpretation, not the availability of the documents for comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original model–hardware optimization simulations, CarbonCLIP evaluations on 41 benchmarks, pruning experiments, and carbon-cost analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains those results and adds language and vision model experiments, regional carbon analyses, fixed-GPU searches, and measurements on V100, A100, and H100 hardware.

M1.justification: The specified pipeline retains importance-based pruning, fine-tuning accuracy proxies, Ax/BoTorch qNEHVI optimization, four objective combinations, and the same hardware/carbon estimation tools. Additional model families and GPU experiments apply this framework; no distinct new algorithmic component or revised CLIP training procedure is established.

E1.justification: v3 adds language-model semantic-similarity evaluation using GLUE/MRPC and standalone ViT classification using CIFAR-10. CIFAR-10 already appeared within v1's CLIP benchmarks, but its role in vision-model fine-tuning and search is new. Appendix K also adds deployment scenarios spanning Taiwan, California, and British Columbia. Existing CLIP training data and 41 evaluation benchmarks remain.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same CLIP and TinyCLIP variants, including CLIP-L/14 and CLIP-H/14 in Table 2. Carbon, energy, latency, and joint carbon–latency optimization remain the comparator modes. Their extension to additional models does not introduce a new comparator; expanded discussion of other NAS methods is not an evaluated baseline addition.

E3.justification: v3 introduces additional backbone configurations, model search with fixed V100-like hardware, and validation against actual V100/A100/H100 measurements using constant-rescaled predictions (Appendices L–M). This substantially extends v1's estimator-validation protocol, which compared CLIP QKV latency estimates with SCALE-Sim. Retained CLIP search and training budgets are not shown to have changed.

E4.justification: Appendices K–M add operational-region sensitivity tests, comparisons of carbon versus energy optimization under different grid intensities, a fixed-GPU case study, and empirical estimator validation. These test environmental dependence and hardware applicability beyond v1. The original pruning, proxy-correlation, compute-budget, and latency-constraint analyses are retained or relocated.

E5.justification: v1 already reported three repetitions and the proxy's Spearman correlation. v3 newly tabulates hypervolume means, standard deviations, and coefficients of variation across model/objective combinations (Table 8), and reports GPU rank correlations with a p < 0.05 statement. This substantially expands statistical reporting without establishing an increase in repeated runs.

E6.justification: Matched CLIP tables, including all 41 benchmark rows, retain their numerical contents. v3 adds non-CLIP trade-offs, regional outcomes, and GPU validation results. Its expanded-model summary reports 30% carbon reduction with 7.7× latency, while GPU validation reports approximately 8% energy and 9% latency error after rescaling. These are additional results, not same-setting improvements over v1; inconsistencies in Tables 5–7 limit their precise interpretation.

T1.justification: Neither version develops formal theoretical results or proofs. The underlying carbon accounting and energy–latency relationship remain unchanged. The new explanation of standard hypervolume statistics does not introduce a substantive mathematical derivation or formal property.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion broaden demonstrated applicability from CLIP to language, vision, and multimodal Transformers. The headline changes from up to 17% carbon reduction for CarbonCLIP to up to 30% across Transformers while claiming maintained accuracy and latency; the original CarbonCLIP claim remains. v3 also explicitly claims the first open-source holistic co-design toolchain.

C2.justification: v3 qualifies energy optimization's latency benefits using BERT/Llama results and explains why cleaner grids strengthen the importance of embodied-carbon optimization. Section 5 adds substantive limitations concerning proxy overfitting, limited GPU support, untested model families, search scalability, and environmental impacts beyond carbon. v1 primarily offered a brief future-work statement.

D1.justification: v3 adds a source-code repository link, supplementary-code availability statements, HuggingFace weight sources, additional configuration tables, and search-runtime estimates. It newly specifies six operating hours per day and documents rescaling in GPU validation, although the scaling constants are not supplied. These are documentation and access-information changes; they do not establish that retained CLIP experiments were rerun.

R1.justification: Related work expands substantially through dedicated edge-AI discussion and additional literature on training emissions, inference energy, language models, and pruning. v3 sharpens its positioning against already-cited CORDOBA and CE-NAS by emphasizing open-source availability and total deployment carbon rather than search emissions. This exceeds citation-style or bibliographic changes.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and framework exposition are extensively rewritten around broader Transformer applicability. Experimental settings and results are combined under Evaluation, joint search precedes fixed-model search, and the impact discussion becomes a limitations section. Appendices are reorganized, a NeurIPS checklist is added, and inconsistent CarbonNaaS terminology is replaced.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a different document template and substantially restructures displays. It combines the pruning and hardware diagrams, expands the iso-accuracy figure to four model panels, relocates proxy and Pareto plots to appendices, and adds regional plots, GPU-validation panels, and statistical tables. Retained tables are restyled and some rows reordered without numerical changes.

improvement.justification: v3 adds useful regional tests, GPU validation, variability reporting, code-access information, and explicit limitations while preserving v1's CLIP evidence. However, its expanded central evidence has unresolved reporting problems: Tables 5–7 repeat identical carbon/latency series, including 26 kgCO2e entries, and Table 6 names Llama2-7B while Section 4.1 specifies Llama3-8B. The headline claim of maintained latency is also not clearly reconciled with Section 4.2's 7.7× latency cost. These substantive gains and reliability concerns prevent a confident net quality judgment.
